reasoning: Both round-4 findings are answered: the unasked auto-merge needs the approval ruleset unchanged too, and the PR body that carries the consent is written by a planned task, kept current on reruns, and asserted by a test.

simpler.evidence: design.md D1 rejects standard commands in SKILL step 5 (non-idempotent ruleset POST, invitation id lookup, token kept out of output); D3 rejects a caller-passed --agent; Standard approach rejects settings-as-code. Round 4's D2 drops both questions per the person's decision; no simpler consent carrier than the PR body the run already writes.

platform.evidence: design.md Standard approach records by command (gh 2.87.3, 2026-11-13) the updateProjectV2Collaborators input and roles, gh auth status --json hosts fields, the autoMergeAllowed unknown field, and live the bot's own-token read of viewerCanUpdate true and viewerPermission WRITE after the Writer role; reference pages cover rulesets, allow_auto_merge, collaborators, invitations, Project access and gh auth token. The approval read-back by re-planning rests on the server keeping the owned fields: this review's read of this repository's live 'agent-process person approves' ruleset (gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets/<id>, person's token) returned include ['~DEFAULT_BRANCH'], bypass_actors [], enforcement active and the template's pull_request parameters, plus server-added keys (allowed_merge_methods, require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes, required_reviewers) that owned_fields ignores (activate_protection.py:157-176), so plan reads it unchanged.

replaced.evidence: D2 lists the two dropped yeses and what now covers each. The writes outside the PR are consented to by starting install, each reversible and printed; the spec now says so instead of claiming the merge covers them. The post-merge writes are covered by the PR body at the merge. The unasked `gh pr merge --auto` now needs both `approval-ruleset` and `auto-merge` `unchanged` (spec, both scenarios, D2 citing ADR 0040 D7, tasks 1.3/3.1), so an earlier install with auto-merge allowed and no approval ruleset is asked only to merge. D3 (agent-account input), D4 (PR read by head, both read-backs) and D5 (auto-merge after approval-ruleset, agent only) hold.

catcher.evidence: The PR body is the consent carrier. D2 and task 2.2 classify post_merge before onboarding and pass its `after-merge` lines to onboarding._pr_step, and onboarding.py is in Impact. A confirmed run that meets the open PR with another list rewrites the body with `gh pr edit --body`; that write falls under *Init runs the post-merge steps*, which the remote-writes requirement admits. test_post_merge_waits_for_the_merge asserts both the body and the rerun edit. Writes that appear only after the merge (a bot added later) follow the person's own act on the `manual agent-identity` row's fix. Other catchers trace: a conflict exits 2 before any write; a read-back mismatch exits non-zero; step 5's rerun prints unchanged; an organisation refusal raises InstallError and exits 1; agent-token conflicts unless git ignores the file.

length.evidence: Added or edited requirement bodies (words): Init runs the post-merge steps ~270, Init finds the agent account 68, Init's remote writes 145, Install's admin steps 41, Install reports a pending agent identity 63, A Claude session start reports a missing agent identity 72, Install continues past the installation PR 163, An upgrade's PR approval ~75, The person's approval merges 41. Every clause has an asserting test in 1.2/1.3: order, after-merge and unchanged conditions, both read-backs (fake serves both rulesets back), the kept keys of a settings file in another form, the check-ignore and non-object conflicts, token absence, call identities, agent account choice, and the SKILL phrases. The untested form clause is gone. The PR-body clause, including the rerun edit, is asserted by test_post_merge_waits_for_the_merge; the confirm-unasked, approval-ruleset-and-auto-merge gate and non-zero-dry-run clauses by test_upgrade_approval_is_its_consent.
